title: Model Harbor: automated intake escrow, variant reconciliation, and runtime acceptance tests
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Build an end-to-end pipeline that reliably ingests externally-supplied OSS model weights into Redwood’s canonical artifact store, performs deterministic conversion to supported runtimes (float16/INT8 paths), reconciles multi-file/variant manifests, signs and escrow-checks artifacts, produces a runtime performance profile, and publishes a pin + profile to the model catalog only after smoke acceptance.

Scope: weights ingestion service + canonicalization worker, checksum and provenance escrow, multi-variant reconciliation (opt/pt/full checkpoints), conversion microservice (with quantization presets), deterministic smoke validation (latency/correctness with small prompt-suite), automated profile publisher, and operator dashboard hooks for failed validations.

Acceptance criteria:
- Ingested artifacts are stored in an escrow bucket with SHA256 manifests and provenance metadata.
- Conversion produces repeatable artifacts with checksum-stable outputs for the same input and config.
- Variant reconciliation merges multiple shard/formats into a single canonical artifact or records a variant family when incompatible.
- Smoke validation verifies model produces expected embeddings/generation on a suite of 12 prompts within thresholds; failures block publish.
- Telemetry emitted for every pipeline stage (time, resource, failure reason) and surfaced in Console.
- Successful runs automatically create a canonical pin and publish a performance profile entry in the catalog.
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Spike completed for escrow layout and manifest schema; Confluence doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/MODEL/Model+Harbor+Escrow+Schema (prototype manifest v0.1)
2026-02-27: Conversion microservice scaffolded (Go) with plugin interface for quant backend; initial float16 path implemented and tested locally against llama-weights sample.

2026-03-03: Variant reconciliation algorithm drafted; uses shard-hash grouping + shape-first compatibility check. Edge-case handling for optimizer states discussed with infra (see meeting notes in doc).

2026-03-05: PR opened for escrow uploader (GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-harbor/pull/112). Running CI: integration tests failing on large-file multipart for a specific S3 gateway in staging.
2026-03-09: Smoke validation harness implemented in Python; initial test suite of 12 prompts, includes both embedding similarity checks and token-level generation smoke tests.
review_feedback: 2026-03-06 - PM review (Jordan Patel): Prefer conservative publish gating; require both smoke and throughput sanity checks before pining.
2026-03-07 - Security (Maya Singh): Add KMS-wrapped manifest signing and retention policy to escrow bucket. Also require RBAC control for publishing to catalog.
2026-03-10 - Runtime lead (Diego Ramos): For INT8 path we need kernel compatibility metadata to decide fallback; add 'kernel-compat' tag to profile output.
testing_plan: Unit tests for manifest parser, checksum validator, and shard assembler.
End-to-end functional test using a synthetic 4-shard model with two variants (FP16 / INT8) in staging; verify canonicalization and smoke pass.
Performance smoke: measure 95th percentile latency on sample prompts (seq length 256) against runtime-1.22 benchmark harness.
Negative tests: corrupted shard, missing metadata, and unsupported architecture to ensure pipeline fails safely and surfaces actionable errors to operators.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): run ingestion + conversion for non-catalog models only; operator approval required to publish pin.
Phase 2 (automated): enable auto-publish for models that pass smoke + throughput sanity and have kernel-compat confirmed.
Rollback: maintain last-known-good profile entry; if publish causes regressions, automatic demote + notify owners + revert pin.
notes: Trade-off: Eager merging of variants simplifies catalog UX but may hide incompatibilities; chosen approach is to create a 'variant family' metadata record when merging is lossy.
Decision: Use SHA256 of canonicalized tensor bytes + config JSON as the artifact fingerprint to maximize determinism across conversion runs.
Open: Need SRE alignment on staging S3 gateway limits; current multipart timeout causes intermittent CI flakes on >5GB artifacts.
